news.headline: ‘What is your fear?': Madras HC pulls up Tamil Nadu govt over denying RSS march
news.story_lead: ‘What is your fear?': Madras HC pulls up Tamil Nadu govt over denying RSS march The court criticised the government's approach towards public demonstrations, saying it appeared to treat citizens as adversaries. The Madras High Court on Wednesday questioned the Tamil Nadu government's repeated refusal to allow the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to hold route marches, pointing out that the organisation had been permitted to conduct such events even in Jammu and Kashmir. "If they (RSS) is able to have a march in a terrorist infested place like Jammu and Kashmir, why is the Tamil Nadu police denying permission to them every year?" the court orally asked, as per LiveLaw .
news.full_article_text: ‘What is your fear?': Madras HC pulls up Tamil Nadu govt over denying RSS march The court criticised the government's approach towards public demonstrations, saying it appeared to treat citizens as adversaries. The Madras High Court on Wednesday questioned the Tamil Nadu government's repeated refusal to allow the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to hold route marches, pointing out that the organisation had been permitted to conduct such events even in Jammu and Kashmir. "If they (RSS) is able to have a march in a terrorist infested place like Jammu and Kashmir, why is the Tamil Nadu police denying permission to them every year?" the court orally asked, as per LiveLaw . Justice V Lakshminarayanan observed that the state government was refusing permission for processions organised by different groups, including the RSS and Dravidar Kazhagam, leaving them with no option but to approach the court. According to Bar and Bench, Justice V Lakshminarayanan asked the Tamil Nadu Advocate General, “What is your fear? Are you fearing...?” "This government is against any procession. They're denying permission for Dravidar Kazhagam and for RSS," the court orally remarked. The court also criticised the government's approach towards public demonstrations, saying it appeared to treat citizens as adversaries. It further noted that RSS route marches continued to face rejection regardless of which government was in power. "The government is seeing citizens as enemies. Whichever government is coming up, they're rejecting," the court orally further said as per LiveLaw . RSS approaches court over October route marches The observations came during the hearing of a petition filed by RSS member VG Jagadeesan. He sought directions to the police to consider his representation and grant permission for route marches on October 18, October 25, November 1, or any other dates. The proposed marches would involve participants wearing the organisation's uniform, accompanied by a musical band, followed by a public meeting. Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate NL Rajah told the court that the organisation faced refusals every year and was repeatedly compelled to seek judicial intervention. He said the RSS wanted to mark its founding day, which coincides with the Vijayadashmi celebration, through a route march. Rajah submitted that the police had denied permission on the grounds that the event could lead to law and order problems. He also raised concerns about smaller political groups that may not have the resources to pursue legal proceedings to secure permission for similar events. "An organisation like the RSS is able to come to court and seek permission. But what about the smaller parties which do not have the wherewithal to come to court?" Rajah asked. State cites restrictions on public meeting venues Advocate General Vijaya Narayan, representing the state, told the court that permission had been refused because the organisers wanted to hold a route march and public meeting at a location that had not been notified as a venue for public meetings. After hearing both sides, the court asked the petitioners' counsel to meet State Public Prosecutor John Sathyan to work out a solution. It directed five members representing the petitioner to meet the prosecutor and find a way to ensure that the proposed meeting could be held peacefully. The court adjourned the matter to Thursday and asked the state to submit a report on allowing a peaceful procession. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Shivya Kanojia Shivya Kanojia is a journalist at Hindustan Times, where she works in the fast-paced digital news ecosystem with a strong sense of editorial judgement and a clear understanding of what makes a story both important and traffic-driven. An alumna of the Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC), Shivya brings a thoughtful balance of news value and audience relevance to her work, ensuring stories resonate beyond the immediate headline. Over the course of her three-year journey in the digital news space, Shivya has worked across a wide range of beats, including politics, civic issues, human-interest features and trending news. This diverse exposure has shaped her ability to approach stories with nuance, adaptability and context, whether she is breaking down complex developments or spotlighting everyday narratives that often go unnoticed. She is particularly drawn to human-interest stories, interviews and explainers that offer depth and clarity, aiming to move past surface-level reporting to explore the people, emotions and circumstances behind the news. RSS approaches court over October route marches The observations came during the hearing of a petition filed by RSS member VG Jagadeesan. He sought directions to the police to consider his representation and grant permission for route marches on October 18, October 25, November 1, or any other dates. The proposed marches would involve participants wearing the organisation's uniform, accompanied by a musical band, followed by a public meeting. Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate NL Rajah told the court that the organisation faced refusals every year and was repeatedly compelled to seek judicial intervention. He said the RSS wanted to mark its founding day, which coincides with the Vijayadashmi celebration, through a route march. Rajah submitted that the police had denied permission on the grounds that the event could lead to law and order problems. He also raised concerns about smaller political groups that may not have the resources to pursue legal proceedings to secure permission for similar events. "An organisation like the RSS is able to come to court and seek permission. But what about the smaller parties which do not have the wherewithal to come to court?" Rajah asked. After hearing both sides, the court asked the petitioners' counsel to meet State Public Prosecutor John Sathyan to work out a solution. news.headline: Mansa medical store owner who shot dead anti-drug activist caught in Rajasthan: Punjab Police
news.story_lead: Medical store owner accused of killing Punjab anti-drug activist Jhota arrested in Rajasthan: Police Punjab Police said Ashwani Kumar was caught in Salasar, Rajasthan, after the activist's killing triggered protests in Mansa and four others were injured. Ashwani Kumar, the medical store owner who went on the run following accusations that he killed anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh alias Jhota in Punjab’s Mansa district, has been picked up from Rajasthan’s Salasar town 300km away, a Punjab Police officer said. Kumar was caught late last night and is being brought to Mansa, police said.

His arrest was broadcast live on social media. “The deceased’s father has agreed to give his statement before the police. Our team is in the process of lodging an FIR,” the officer said. Kumar’s associate, who allegedly helped Ashwani flee Mansa after the murder, has already been arrested by the police. Also Read: Anti-drug activist shot dead in Punjab's Mansa, was questioning chemist over illegal sale Jhota was shot dead on Tuesday morning when he went to a retail pharmacy outlet in Mansa town and accused the owner of peddling drugs. In a widely circulated video clip, Ashwani was allegedly seen opening fire at Jhota after he made the accusation. HT cannot verify the authenticity of the video. Four others also suffered bullet injuries when Ashwani allegedly fired multiple times in the market. A senior medical officer (SMO), Gurmail Singh, said Jhota suffered two gunshot injuries in the abdomen and one more in the right thigh. A heavy police force was deployed outside the Civil Hospital, where the body was kept. According to PTI, Jhota and his supporters in 2023 garlanded Kumar with shoes and paraded him through the market after a man was found with banned capsules allegedly procured from his shop.

The CM said that it was an issue which affects most of south-central Kerala and not just Kottayam district. "It affects Kottayam, Pathanamthitta and Alappuzha districts and parts of Ernakulam district. He said that the problem is due to the reason that water is not properly flowing into the sea from the lake. It gets collected in many places," he said. As a result, Kuttanad and Upper Kuttanad areas of the state are badly flooded, agriculture there is destroyed and residents are starting to move out. "It is a serious environmental issue and I assure the House that the government will address it on a priority basis by holding discussions to formulate a well-planned project, with a long term view, for renovation of the Vembanad lake and protect the region around it from flooding during the rains," Satheesan said in the assembly. He further said that all this will be carried out in a time bound manner. Meanwhile, Revenue Minister A P Anilkumar and Water Resources Minister Mons Joseph told the assembly that the government was taking steps to undertake mining of sand from rivers and lakes in the state and the process is expected to be completed soon. "So, the removal of sand will commence by December this year or January 2027," Anilkumar said. They were responding to several queries by various MLAs regarding the steps the government proposes to take to address the issue of extensive flooding in their constituencies due to overflowing rivers during the rains. The ministers said that removal of sediments from river beds had not been carried out in the state for the last several years, leading to their carrying capacity being reduced and causing them to overflow during rains. news.headline: CRPF sub-inspector dies by suicide in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur
news.story_lead: CRPF sub-inspector dies by suicide in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur Sukma, A sub-inspector of the Central Reserve Police Force allegedly died by suicide after shooting himself with his service weapon at his unit's camp in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur district, police said on Wednesday. The incident occurred on the intervening night of Monday and Tuesday at Mettagudam camp, located in a forested area of Bijapur district adjoining Sukma, a police official said. Sub-Inspector Devanand Yadav, from the CRPF's 131st battalion, allegedly shot himself with his service weapon for unknown reasons, he said.
news.full_article_text: CRPF sub-inspector dies by suicide in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur Sukma, A sub-inspector of the Central Reserve Police Force allegedly died by suicide after shooting himself with his service weapon at his unit's camp in Chhattisgarh's Bijapur district, police said on Wednesday. The incident occurred on the intervening night of Monday and Tuesday at Mettagudam camp, located in a forested area of Bijapur district adjoining Sukma, a police official said. Sub-Inspector Devanand Yadav, from the CRPF's 131st battalion, allegedly shot himself with his service weapon for unknown reasons, he said. After hearing the gunshot, fellow personnel and officers at the camp provided him immediate first aid and shifted him in a field ambulance to Elmagunda camp in Sukma district, where he died during treatment, the official said. Yadav hailed from Karjaha village in Uttar Pradesh's Deoria district, he said. Police registered a case of unnatural death. news.headline: ‘Where does CJP go when issues arise in other states?’: CM Rekha Gupta amid anti-CEC protests in Delhi
news.story_lead: ‘Where does CJP go when issues arise in other states?’: CM Rekha Gupta amid anti-CEC protests in Delhi Addressing a press conference, the BJP leader questioned whether the pressure group has spoken about issues in other states. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta questioned the Cockroach Janta Party on Wednesday amid the recent protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the capital. Addressing a press conference, the BJP leader questioned whether the pressure group has spoken about issues in other states.
news.full_article_text: ‘Where does CJP go when issues arise in other states?’: CM Rekha Gupta amid anti-CEC protests in Delhi Addressing a press conference, the BJP leader questioned whether the pressure group has spoken about issues in other states. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta questioned the Cockroach Janta Party on Wednesday amid the recent protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the capital. Addressing a press conference, the BJP leader questioned whether the pressure group has spoken about issues in other states. Track LIVE updates on Delhi protests “It is surprising that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is being questioned in this manner, even though it is not being conducted for the first time in the country. Such revisions have been carried out on numerous occasions over the years by the Election Commission. This has been the practice regardless of which party was in power, either at the state or the central level. Why were there no voices raised against it earlier? Why are such objections being raised now?” the Delhi CM told reporters. Deep Dive The chief minister said the protests have caused Delhi "losses worth thousands of crores" and that this disruption is due to the ongoing sit-ins and protests. "You want to oppose the system functioning in a democracy simply because you have failed to form the government. I want to ask... if you form the government in Tamil Nadu or Kerala, will such an exercise not take place there? Does this issue concern you only in states where you have failed to form the government?" Gupta asked. Also Read | Rahul Gandhi backs CJP after Das, Ranka jailed: ‘Waving Tricolour at Jantar Mantar not a crime' She also fired a salvo at CJP, reiterating the BJP's claim that the pressure group is the Aam Aadmi Party's "B-team." "Where does this CJP go when issues arise in those states? Why does it not go there to stage protests? Now, following the murder linked to drugs yesterday, why doesn't CJP go to Punjab and stage a protest? Why does it function as the Aam Aadmi Party's 'B-team', working only on the political agenda conveyed by the Aam Aadmi Party?" Gupta said. Gupta's remarks come after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five-day judicial custody over their breach of Jantar Mantar, which was de-notified as a protest site earlier this week. The CM also hit out at Congress, stating that the party is joining hands with “people abroad who are jealous of India.” “The people of the country are fully satisfied with the development work being carried out under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The country is progressing and strengthening its position on the global stage. This is what troubles them. By joining hands with people abroad who are jealous of India, they continue to work towards harming the country,” Gupta told reporters. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: IIIT Ranchi director sent on leave amid stir after student's suicide
news.story_lead: IIIT Ranchi director sent on leave amid stir after student's suicide It comes a day after the ministry of education instituted a three-member panel to look into issues related to the institution and the students' demands. In an administrative crackdown following prolonged student protests at the Indian Institute of Information Technology, Ranchi (IIIT-Ranchi) after the alleged suicide of a first-year student on Saturday night , the Union ministry of education sent the institute's Director, Rajiv Srivastava, on a 30-day leave with immediate effect, people aware of the development said on Wednesday. The development comes a day after the ministry instituted a three-member panel to look into issues related to the institution and the students' demands.
news.full_article_text: IIIT Ranchi director sent on leave amid stir after student's suicide It comes a day after the ministry of education instituted a three-member panel to look into issues related to the institution and the students' demands. In an administrative crackdown following prolonged student protests at the Indian Institute of Information Technology, Ranchi (IIIT-Ranchi) after the alleged suicide of a first-year student on Saturday night , the Union ministry of education sent the institute's Director, Rajiv Srivastava, on a 30-day leave with immediate effect, people aware of the development said on Wednesday. The development comes a day after the ministry instituted a three-member panel to look into issues related to the institution and the students' demands. To resolve the administrative deadlock, Prof. V. M. S. R. Murthy, the current Director of IIEST Shibpur, has been given the additional charge as the Officiating Director of IIIT Ranchi. Prof. Murthy will head the institution for one month or until further orders. IIIT Registrar in charge, Munuren Samson Champia, confirmed both developments. "The director has proceeded on 30 days' leave as a probe is being done into the complaint against him. V. M. S. R. Murthy has been appointed as officiating director," he said without elaborating details. Protesting students halt stir A protesting IIIT student said they have temporarily halted their strike following the administrative action. "Strike has now ended after the director was shunted for 30 days," the student said. An insider sharing an administrative order said that following the director's 30-day removal, the institute administration has also cancelled the recent recruitment process for various non-teaching posts, which had been mired in controversy. According to an official notice issued by the Registrar in-charge, a copy of which is available with Hindustan Times, the recruitment process stands cancelled with immediate effect due to unavoidable administrative circumstances. The administration confirmed that the application fees paid by candidates will be fully refunded. The official link and necessary instructions for claiming the refund will be uploaded shortly to the institute’s official website. Discussing suicides can be triggering for some. news.exam_corner_topic: Farm fires evading satellite monitoring prompt focussed ground monitoring
news.headline: Farm fires evading satellite monitoring prompt focussed ground monitoring
news.story_lead: Farm fires evading satellite monitoring prompt focussed ground monitoring Air quality in Delhi and NCR starts worsening from mid-September, with stubble burning as a precursor to pollution Farm fires, a major reason for pollution in northwestern India and the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR), have been declining year-on-year. But multiple studies have suggested a trend of farmers setting their fields ablaze after 3pm to evade satellite captures, prompting the government to call for intensified ground-level monitoring. Air quality in Delhi and NCR starts worsening from mid-September, with stubble burning as a precursor to winter pollution.
news.full_article_text: Farm fires evading satellite monitoring prompt focussed ground monitoring Air quality in Delhi and NCR starts worsening from mid-September, with stubble burning as a precursor to pollution Farm fires, a major reason for pollution in northwestern India and the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR), have been declining year-on-year. But multiple studies have suggested a trend of farmers setting their fields ablaze after 3pm to evade satellite captures, prompting the government to call for intensified ground-level monitoring. Air quality in Delhi and NCR starts worsening from mid-September, with stubble burning as a precursor to winter pollution. Smog chokes the Capital every winter. Subsequent fireworks during the festive season, especially around Diwali, worsen the situation despite curbs, which are violated every year. PM2.5 is the dominant pollutant affecting the air quality. Secondary particulates formed from emissions from transport, industries, power plants, and biomass burning are among the major pollution contributors during winter. At a joint review meeting on Tuesday, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav emphasised the need to intensify ground monitoring and enforcement to prevent stubble burning focussed on fires after 3pm. He called for special focus on Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Amritsar, Patiala, and Gurdaspur (Punjab), and Kaithal, Karnal, Kurukshetra, Ambala, and Fatehabad (Haryana) to assess crop-harvesting trends. Deep Dive In a statement, Yadav’s ministry said he underlined that monitoring should not rely solely on satellite data and asked district collectors to conduct on-the-ground assessments and strengthen enforcement action to make efforts to curb crop residue burning more effective. It added that he called for strict monitoring of stubble burning through ground patrolling and flying squads during the satellite monitoring gap window, when satellites do not capture farm fires after 3 pm. Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who attended the joint review meeting, asked for action on a “war footing” to prevent stubble burning, while emphasising the need to provide farmers with easy, accessible and affordable alternatives. He directed that crop residue machines be provided to farmers at the earliest. Chouhan cited data from September 15 to October 12 and said there has been a significant reduction of 53.3% in the incidents of stubble-burning in Haryana and around 32% in Uttar Pradesh compared to last year. He added that Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh remained a cause of concern. He asked the two states to identify affected districts and villages and immediately implement a special action plan. Chouhan said there has been a marginal decline in Punjab farm fires in comparison to the same period last year. Yadav stressed the need to link stubble burning data with that of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) for effective monitoring. He emphasised the importance of providing forecasts of likely harvest times and monitoring meteorological conditions affecting air pollution levels in the NCR so that necessary action can be taken accordingly. States have started deploying drones for the first time to monitor stubble burning in real-time. In July, CAQM issued a standard operating procedure (SOP) and framework for using drones in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan this winter to detect crop-burning incidents. It asked for drone deployment preferably between 3pm and 9pm when farmers are more likely to evade satellite detection. Last year, multiple studies showed farmers burning fields late in the evening to avoid being captured by satellite imagery, resulting in an overall lower farm-fire count. India’s polar-orbiting satellites complete their overpass and capture crop burning incidents typically between 10:30 am and 1:30 pm. Environmental think tank International Forum for Environment, Sustainability and Technology’s study in December 2025 found most fires were lit after 3pm, hours when monitoring systems were not working across Punjab and Haryana. Another Indian Space Research Organisation study noted a similar trend. “We observe a gradual temporal shift between 2021 and 2024, with peak fire activity occurring around 5 PM IST in 2024… At the same time, the window of fire activity narrowed substantially, suggesting an informed adjustment by farmers to avoid detection by polar-orbiting sensors,” said the study published in Current Science in November last year. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. His reports in 2019 on toxic leachate from Delhi's landfills led to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) taking suo motu cognisance and ultimately asking the state government to start bio-mining to flatten and remove all three landfills in the capital. He also closely tracks the implementation of government policies on climate, renewable energy and environmental protection. His focus remains on impactful, public-interest journalism which explains how environmental decisions affect people's everyday lives. Read More - Satellite Monitoring

news.headline: CJP lawyer claims Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka arrested after Jantar Mantar breach, Delhi Police calls it preventive
news.story_lead: CJP lawyer claims Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka arrested after Jantar Mantar breach, Delhi Police calls it preventive Ratna Singh, in an update early on Wednesday, said Das, Ranka and Shinde will likely be produced before a special executive magistrate (SEM) before 7 am. The Cockroach Janta Party has claimed that its co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been arrested, following the Jantar Mantar breach on Tuesday morning. However, the Delhi Police said they were placing the CJP leaders, including Ajinkya Shinde, “under preventive arrest”, ANI news agency reported.
news.full_article_text: CJP lawyer claims Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka arrested after Jantar Mantar breach, Delhi Police calls it preventive Ratna Singh, in an update early on Wednesday, said Das, Ranka and Shinde will likely be produced before a special executive magistrate (SEM) before 7 am. The Cockroach Janta Party has claimed that its co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have been arrested, following the Jantar Mantar breach on Tuesday morning. However, the Delhi Police said they were placing the CJP leaders, including Ajinkya Shinde, “under preventive arrest”, ANI news agency reported. CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh, in an update early on Wednesday, said Das, Ranka and Shinde will likely be produced before a special executive magistrate (SEM) at Mandir Marg Police Station before 7 am. The Delhi Police had, on Tuesday evening, filed an FIR against Das, Ranka and Shinde for allegedly trespassing into the Jantar Mantar area without authorisation, PTI news agency cited officials as saying. What has the CJP said? While the cops say the leaders are under preventive arrest, CJP's Ratna Singh, in a post on X, said the Delhi Police had arrested Das, Ranka and Shinde in the breach case. “Trespass, bond violation, obstruction of public official’s duty, etc,” Singh said about the charges on them. Deep Dive She had also claimed that there was a possibility of “judicial custody in Tihar Jail” after the CJP leaders were presented before the SCM court. “They were not allowed to meet their lawyers till late at night. They were brought to Parliament Street PS at 3 AM in a private van,” Singh claimed. She later also posted a photograph of the three from Parliament Street Police Station. “Despite these illegal actions, their spirits are high,” Singh added. In the update post, Singh said, “FYI, 24 hours timeline will end soon.” Why were the CJP leaders arrested? Das, Ranka and Shinde along with other CJP volunteers had entered Jantar Mantar by jumping the locked gates on Tuesday, a day after the site lost its designated protest venue status. Ranka shared a video of the incident on his X handle, showing Das and him, along with outfit's national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde, climbing the locked gates and entering the venue before police personnel present there intervened and took hold of them. Ranka also displayed the Tricolour at the venue, before Delhi Police detained the CJP leaders. Saurav Das shared a video on his Instagram handle shortly after detention and said, “We have breached Jantar Mantar.” Ashutosh Ranka said in the video that the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar will happen from Jantar Mantar only, "no matter what". - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: Missiles intercepted near Riyadh after Saudi coalition hits Yemen fuel depot
news.story_lead: The Houthi-run Yemen Petroleum Company assured residents of Sanaa that it had sufficient fuel supplies - Published 13 October 2026 Missiles and drones have been intercepted over Riyadh after the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa, its spokesperson says. Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said several projectiles targeting the Saudi capital and other cities were intercepted after the coalition carried out a strike on the Yemen Petroleum Company's al-Sabaha facility on Tuesday night. The Houthis warned they would target the airport and Aramco refinery in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and Aramco's headquarters in the eastern city of Dammam.
news.full_article_text: The Houthi-run Yemen Petroleum Company assured residents of Sanaa that it had sufficient fuel supplies - Published 13 October 2026 Missiles and drones have been intercepted over Riyadh after the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen struck a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa, its spokesperson says. Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said several projectiles targeting the Saudi capital and other cities were intercepted after the coalition carried out a strike on the Yemen Petroleum Company's al-Sabaha facility on Tuesday night. The Houthis warned they would target the airport and Aramco refinery in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and Aramco's headquarters in the eastern city of Dammam. Al-Maliki later said missiles targeting cities including Dammam had been intercepted, while shrapnel had fallen in a residential area in Dhahran. An Armaco administration building in Dhahran was also targeted, resulting in "limited fire", Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy said in a statement. No casualties were reported, the statement said. It came as the Saudi cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, said the Iran-backed group would "bear the consequences" of its recent deadly attacks on the kingdom. Thirteen people were killed when a missile hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, while another person was killed in a similar attack there the following day. On Tuesday, the coalition said its forces had destroyed three drones north of Riyadh. The Houthis have said they are targeting airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones in response to deadly Saudi strikes on territory that they control in western Yemen, including Sanaa. The Saudi-led coalition has been providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces mounting an offensive on Yemen's Red Sea coast and several other front lines. A correspondent for AFP news agency reported that queues formed at petrol stations in Sanaa on Tuesday afternoon following the coalition's warning of an impending operation against the al-Sabaha oil facility, with many residents worried about shortages. The Yemen Petroleum Company, which is run by the Houthis, issued a statement that sought to reassure them, saying the facility "does not contain any stock of petroleum products". The company also said it had "taken all necessary precautionary measures to address any emergency, ensuring the stability of the supply situation and the continued meeting of citizens' needs in a normal manner". After al-Maliki confirmed the strike, first reported by Houthi media, explosions were heard over Riyadh and other Saudi cities, with al-Maliki reporting four missiles and two drones had been intercepted near the capital. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran. US President Donald Trump said on Truth Social on Tuesday the Houthis were "behaving very badly... and purposefully trying to drive up Oil Prices". Speaking to reporters, he did not answer a question on whether he'd made a decision to help the Saudis retaliate against them, but said he "might" ask Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan to intervene. Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes. Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed in Yemen since August. The UN's human rights office says they include at least 54 civilians, half of them children. More than 216,000 people have also been displaced across the country, and suspected cholera cases have tripled in three weeks, rising from 217 to 647, according to the UN. news.full_article_text: Manipur police arrest 13, including a minor for circulating non-consensual explicit videos of women A suo motu case was registered under relevant sections of the Information Technology Act, Pocso Act, and BNS Manipur police arrested 13 people, including a minor, for allegedly circulating and monetising non-consensual explicit videos and photographs of local women, including child sexual abuse material (CSAM), through multiple Telegram channels and WhatsApp groups, police said on Tuesday. A senior police officer on Tuesday said that the accused were arrested on Monday night following an investigation under Operation Dignity, which was launched after the police received credible information about channels allegedly involved in circulating such material, including CSAM. A suo motu case was registered under relevant sections of the Information Technology Act, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). During the investigation, a police team led by Leishangthem Jeebit Singh, sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) of Moirang in Bishnupur district, recovered and seized 14 mobile phones and a laptop allegedly used to commit the offences. Also Read: Manipur hill districts remain tense after Kamjong clashes, bodies of victims handed to kin The investigation revealed that Telegram channels and WhatsApp groups were allegedly being used to distribute sexually explicit content, with access sold to subscribers. Many of the clips reportedly featured women from Manipur who had not consented to their distribution. A police statement said, “The investigation indicates the network is organised, profit-driven, and self-sustaining, with subscriber demand encouraging further recording and release.” According to the statement, administrators used teaser previews on open platforms to attract subscribers, charging between ₹ 150 and ₹ 500 through digital payment platforms before providing access to private groups. A senior police officer, requesting anonymity, told HT that the investigation had uncovered “an organised secondary market fuelled by non-consensual leaks, hacking, and in several instances, direct production and grave non-consensual sexual exploitation by the accused”. The officer said the police identified more than 150 active Telegram channels and WhatsApp groups and had neutralised 38 of them. “We have recovered more than 6,000 video clips, and many of them were found to have been captured using hidden cameras, AI-generated content and other means without the consent of the victims,” the officer said. “It was also found that most of the videos were taken using hidden cameras and mobile phones in restrooms, hotels and changing rooms,” the officer added. The officer said most of the accused were college students, school dropouts, labourers and employees of private institutions. The officer added that more people could be involved in the alleged crimes. “As the investigation is underway, no further information can be provided about the accused or victims,” the officer said. The arrested persons have been identified as N Rajesh Singh alias Maipakchao (21), from Bishnupur; H Dhanajit Singh alias Taison (19), from Bishnupur; S Saphaba Singh (19), from Imphal West; Th Cavendish Singh alias Ingocha (21), from Kakching; H Rojit Singh (19), from Bishnupur; M Clinton Singh (28), from Bishnupur; Kh Bipin Singh (31), from Thoubal; S Simpson Singh (34), from Imphal West; A Aria Singh (24), from Bishnupur; S Alexander Singh (31), from Kakching; K Rakesh Singh (18), from Imphal West; Ch Robert Singh (27), from Imphal West; and one child in conflict with the law. The police statement said the investigation was underway to establish the wider network, trace financial transactions and identify additional victims. In an advisory issued on Tuesday, Bishnupur police warned the public against possessing, circulating, forwarding or hosting non-consensual intimate media and CSAM, stating that such acts could attract criminal prosecution under applicable laws. The police also cautioned that paying subscription fees to access private groups did not guarantee anonymity and that subscribers could face prosecution if found to be involved in the alleged network. The public has been urged not to forward teaser clips, previews or group links and to report offending accounts and links to the police. Parents and guardians have been advised to monitor children’s online activities, particularly on Telegram and WhatsApp, and encourage them to report uncomfortable behaviour, unauthorised image leaks, hacking or online blackmail. The police assured victims that their identities will remain protected in accordance with statutory requirements. They also said assistance will be provided to facilitate content removal through StopNCII and platform-level takedown mechanisms, along with access to legal aid, trauma counselling and state victim compensation support. The statement further warned that investigators were tracing digital evidence, including UPI transactions, bank accounts, QR payment records and device identifiers, to identify others allegedly involved in the network.

The officer added that more people could be involved in the alleged crimes. “As the investigation is underway, no further information can be provided about the accused or victims,” the officer said. The police statement said the investigation was underway to establish the wider network, trace financial transactions and identify additional victims. In an advisory issued on Tuesday, Bishnupur police warned the public against possessing, circulating, forwarding or hosting non-consensual intimate media and CSAM, stating that such acts could attract criminal prosecution under applicable laws. The police also cautioned that paying subscription fees to access private groups did not guarantee anonymity and that subscribers could face prosecution if found to be involved in the alleged network. The public has been urged not to forward teaser clips, previews or group links and to report offending accounts and links to the police. Parents and guardians have been advised to monitor children’s online activities, particularly on Telegram and WhatsApp, and encourage them to report uncomfortable behaviour, unauthorised image leaks, hacking or online blackmail. The police assured victims that their identities will remain protected in accordance with statutory requirements. They also said assistance will be provided to facilitate content removal through StopNCII and platform-level takedown mechanisms, along with access to legal aid, trauma counselling and state victim compensation support. The statement further warned that investigators were tracing digital evidence, including UPI transactions, bank accounts, QR payment records and device identifiers, to identify others allegedly involved in the network.

news.headline: Can new transport authority tackle siloed planning gaps?
news.story_lead: Can new transport authority tackle siloed planning gaps? India’s new transport authority aims to coordinate infrastructure planning, but experts say its impact hinges on real powers, reliable data and travel demand. Khajuraho Airport in Madhya Pradesh secured the joint top position in the Airports Authority of India’s customer satisfaction survey for January-June 2026, with a score of 4.98 out of 5.
news.full_article_text: Can new transport authority tackle siloed planning gaps? India’s new transport authority aims to coordinate infrastructure planning, but experts say its impact hinges on real powers, reliable data and travel demand. Khajuraho Airport in Madhya Pradesh secured the joint top position in the Airports Authority of India’s customer satisfaction survey for January-June 2026, with a score of 4.98 out of 5. Incidentally, scheduled commercial flights from the airport stopped on July 1, before the survey results were out. The development illustrates the mismatch between infrastructure provision and actual travel demand, with experts describing the practice of planning and building transport infrastructure as individualised, tokenised projects rather than parts of a larger plan on journeys people and goods make. The Union Cabinet’s October 6 approval of the Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) has raised expectations among policy observers that India could move towards more coordinated planning of roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways and urban mobility. The authority is mandated to prepare a National Transport Master Plan with a horizon of at least 10 years, and will test ministries’ annual and shorter-term sectoral plans against it. It will also appraise central infrastructure projects costing ₹ 500 crore or more, monitor their implementation and assess their impact after completion. Whether it can deliver, experts say, will turn on the powers it is given. A senior government official with experience across more than one transport-sector ministry at the Centre, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said departments often plan to expand their own networks without adequately accounting for investments being made by others. He said at different meetings within the government, the example of Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism has been cited, which was created following a merger in 2001. “A railway line, highway or waterway may each be justified within its sector’s plans, but the connections between them can be overlooked. Everybody is trying to increase their own share from the same pie without looking at which is the most beneficial for the end user or the most resource-smart,” the official said. The result, the official said, can be overlapping projects and infrastructure that does not connect properly with the wider network. “First- and last-mile links are a particular weakness. For example, a freight terminal or railway station may be built without adequate road connectivity to bring goods or passengers to it.” Power, or the lack of it Without powers to halt funding for individual projects, ITLA’s influence remains uncertain. Jagan Shah, professor of practice at IIT Delhi’s Transportation Research and Injury Prevention Centre, said the authority would need veto powers to make its broad mandate effective. “Unless the authority has veto power — the mandate to review projects and, where necessary, veto them — it risks being unable to influence decisions,” Shah said, warning that a lack of powers, resources and independence could undermine both the public interest and the authority’s functioning. Shah also raised questions about how ITLA would work with state and local agencies, particularly development authorities, whose responsibilities could overlap with its planning mandate. He cited the UK’s National Infrastructure Commission as an example of an independent body that can publicly challenge the government on infrastructure decisions. Only as good as its data ITLA’s ability to compare projects will also depend on the quality of the information available to it. It is expected to build a National Transport Data Repository by bringing together data from Goods and Services Tax Network e-way bills, FASTag, VAHAN, global positioning systems and urban traffic management systems. The government says the repository will support freight-flow and origin-destination analysis for planning, monitoring and impact assessment. Shah said the repository would need to be regularly updated and access to its data governed transparently. If information is incomplete or accessible only to selected users, he warned, it would create uncompetitive markets that would hurt economic growth in the medium and long term. Pawan Mulukutla, executive programme director for integrated transport, clean air and hydrogen at WRI India, said the authority should include industry representatives and independent experts to ensure decisions reflect operational realities. “Different transport modes should complement rather than compete with one another, with choices guided by geography, the type of goods being moved, journey requirements, cost and efficiency.” He said all investment decisions must be tested against the economics of moving people and goods, with scope to use modelling and artificial intelligence-based tools to assess which transport modes would work best for particular routes and types of freight. Capex vs service-oriented approach The need for coordination has been recognised for years. Ravi Gadepalli, founder of Transit Intelligence, a public transport consultancy, said the idea of an integrated transport ministry has been around for a long time, “But it is difficult for institutions (different ministries) to give up independent decision-making powers.” Gadepalli hopes the ITLA can be a via-media solution where ministries retain their powers but coordinate on project specific matters. “The ILTA may go-beyond co-ordination and execute projects which are not within any individual ministry’s mandate such as building a multimodal hub connecting a railway station with a bus station, where separate agencies may have to build different components and secure permissions from one another.” For passenger transport, that means looking beyond new roads and rail infrastructure to how people actually travel between and within cities. “Transport sector spending remains skewed towards building infrastructure rather than providing services. Highways are treated as development expenditure, while buses and railways are often expected to recover their costs through fares, even when affordable services require continuing public funding support,” he said. To make the case for changing this approach, Gadepalli pointed to a 2020 policy brief by the International Association of Public Transport (UITP), which he co-authored. The study compared the employment and mobility benefits of different investments. For every ₹ 10,000 crore invested in 2016-17, improving public bus services was estimated to generate 110.4 million man-days of employment and provide access to 10.6 billion passenger-trips, against 3.2 million man-days and 2.8 billion passenger-trips for road infrastructure development. He said slowly the approach is changing with rollout of schemes such as PM-eBus Sewa but a larger and more systematic transition from road building to bus service improvement is needed at the natio

news.headline: flydubai 'hijack' bid probe widens as 2 Maldivian pilots arrested in UAE over links to Omani co-pilot: Report
news.story_lead: flydubai 'hijack' bid probe widens as 2 Maldivian pilots arrested in UAE over links to Omani co-pilot: Report The two pilots were taken into custody on October 3, and their families have been formally notified of their detention by the Maldivian Embassy in the UAE. Two Maldivian pilots working for flydubai have been arrested in the United Arab Emirates in connection with an alleged attempt to hijack and crash a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, media reports said. The case relates to a September 30 incident in which Indian Captain Smit Machchhar was injured while resisting an alleged attack by an Omani co-pilot.
news.full_article_text: flydubai 'hijack' bid probe widens as 2 Maldivian pilots arrested in UAE over links to Omani co-pilot: Report The two pilots were taken into custody on October 3, and their families have been formally notified of their detention by the Maldivian Embassy in the UAE. Two Maldivian pilots working for flydubai have been arrested in the United Arab Emirates in connection with an alleged attempt to hijack and crash a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, media reports said. The case relates to a September 30 incident in which Indian Captain Smit Machchhar was injured while resisting an alleged attack by an Omani co-pilot. The two pilots were taken into custody on October 3, and their families have been formally notified of their detention by the Maldivian Embassy in the UAE, Maldivian news portal Adhadhu reported. Authorities in the Maldives have not commented on the arrests. The UAE has also not released official details about the allegations against the two men or clarified whether investigators have established their involvement in the suspected plot. What is known about the arrested pilots According to the Male-based newspaper Mihaaru, as quoted by news agency PTI, the two pilots are believed to have interacted with Hammam al-Hammami, the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Machchhar, at their workplace. They are also reported to have lived in the same building as him. However, authorities have not disclosed the nature of their alleged links to the incident or the evidence, if any, against them. News portal edition.mv reported that the two men are among six Maldivian nationals employed as pilots by flydubai. They are also reportedly the airline's most recent recruits from the Maldives. The arrests came as UAE authorities expanded their investigation into the alleged attempt to seize control of flight FZ1073 and crash the aircraft. How the alleged mid-air attack unfolded Flight FZ1073 was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 passengers and crew members on board when the alleged attack took place on September 30. Reportedly, al-Hammami allegedly attacked Machchhar with an axe and stabbed him in an attempt to take control of the aircraft and carry out a "terrorist attack". Despite being seriously injured, Machchhar resisted the alleged assault and managed to unlock the cockpit door. Crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit, overpowered the co-pilot and helped stabilise the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing at Tabuk airport in Saudi Arabia. news.headline: Mamata Banerjee escapes knife attack, TMC claims assailant was a 'drug addict, posed as her niece'
news.story_lead: Mamata Banerjee escapes knife attack, TMC claims assailant was a 'drug addict, posed as her niece' Party MP Dola Sen sent a written complaint to the Kalighat police station in Kolkata stating that the incident took place around 6 pm. A woman who claimed to be a niece of former chief minister Mamata Banerjee allegedly tried to enter her security cordon with a knife in an intoxicated state on Tuesday evening, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress claimed. Party MP Dola Sen sent a written complaint to the Kalighat police station in Kolkata stating that the incident took place around 6 pm near Banerjee’s residence in Kalighat.
news.full_article_text: Mamata Banerjee escapes knife attack, TMC claims assailant was a 'drug addict, posed as her niece' Party MP Dola Sen sent a written complaint to the Kalighat police station in Kolkata stating that the incident took place around 6 pm. A woman who claimed to be a niece of former chief minister Mamata Banerjee allegedly tried to enter her security cordon with a knife in an intoxicated state on Tuesday evening, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress claimed. Party MP Dola Sen sent a written complaint to the Kalighat police station in Kolkata stating that the incident took place around 6 pm near Banerjee’s residence in Kalighat. “This is to inform you that around 6 pm on Tuesday, a lady named Tannishtha Saha, reportedly known as a civic volunteer and a drug addict, came with a violent mode and attacked Mamata Banerjee with a knife and furthermore claimed herself as her niece,” Sen stated in her letter to the officer-in-charge of Kalighat police station. Banerjee had come out of her house to inaugurate a Durga Puja pandal near her residence when the woman tried to enter the security cordon from behind. “When I asked her identity, she said that Banerjee was her paternal aunt. I refused to let her in. She then tried to sneak into the security cordon from the front. When she failed, she lay down on the road and started hurling abuses. It was then that we saw that she had a knife,” Sen said. A TMC leader said that the woman was overpowered by TMC workers around Banerjee and later handed over to the police. No senior police officials, including Rahul De, deputy commissioner of police (south), responded to calls and messages.

news.headline: Delhi Police file FIR against CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others for ‘trespassing’ into Jantar Mantar
news.story_lead: Delhi Police file FIR against CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others for ‘trespassing’ into Jantar Mantar The action came hours after Das, Ranka were detained for entering the heavily barricaded protest site and raising slogans demanding CEC's resignation. Delhi Police on Tuesday filed a First Information Report (FIR) against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and its other members for allegedly trespassing into the Jantar Mantar area without authorisation. The action came hours after Das, Ranka were detained for entering the heavily barricaded protest site by jumping the locked gates and raising slogans demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
news.full_article_text: Delhi Police file FIR against CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others for ‘trespassing’ into Jantar Mantar The action came hours after Das, Ranka were detained for entering the heavily barricaded protest site and raising slogans demanding CEC's resignation. Delhi Police on Tuesday filed a First Information Report (FIR) against Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and its other members for allegedly trespassing into the Jantar Mantar area without authorisation. The action came hours after Das, Ranka were detained for entering the heavily barricaded protest site by jumping the locked gates and raising slogans demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Ranka shared a video on his X handle, showing him and Das, along with outfit's national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde, climbing the locked gates of Jantar Mantar and entering the venue before police personnel present there intervened and took hold of them. Deep Dive Saurav Das said on X later that they have been “taken away to Jaffarpur Police Station.” Jantar Mantar loses protest site status Jantar Mantar was denotified as a protest site on Monday, a Delhi Police circular stated. It also listed three new sites — spread out across the city — for holding demonstrations. According to the circular, the Ministry of Home Affairs had constituted a committee to examine alternative proper venues for citizen's right for organizing protest/demonstrations in place of the existing "designated site". Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground, in Shahdara, have been designated as new venues for organising protest and demonstrations. Reacting to the denotification order, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the entire country will become Jantar Mantar now. “They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it’s no a longer protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega! [entire country will become Jantar Mantar now],” he wrote on X. We reclaimed it: Dipke Following the trespassing incident, Dipke took to X and said, “Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police." “You cannot denotify the resistance,” Dipke said on his X post after the detention of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde for entering Jantar Mantar. Das also shared a video on his Instagram handle shortly after detention and said, “We have breached Jantar Mantar.” Ashutosh Ranka said in the video that the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar will happen from Jantar Mantar only, "no matter what". news.headline: 11 dead, several missing after boat capsizes in Bihar’s Raghopur
news.story_lead: 11 dead, several missing after boat capsizes in Bihar’s Raghopur Around 25 to 30 people were reportedly aboard the medium-sized boat, most of them travelling to attend a feast organised as part of Hindu funeral rituals. At least 11 people, all minors under the age of 18, have died and several others are missing after a boat capsized in the Ganga near Rampur Shyamchand village in Bihar’s Vaishali district on Tuesday evening. Vaishali District Magistrate Varsha Singh said seven people had been rescued, including the boat owner, and that rescue operations would continue through the night.
news.full_article_text: 11 dead, several missing after boat capsizes in Bihar’s Raghopur Around 25 to 30 people were reportedly aboard the medium-sized boat, most of them travelling to attend a feast organised as part of Hindu funeral rituals. At least 11 people, all minors under the age of 18, have died and several others are missing after a boat capsized in the Ganga near Rampur Shyamchand village in Bihar’s Vaishali district on Tuesday evening. Vaishali District Magistrate Varsha Singh said seven people had been rescued, including the boat owner, and that rescue operations would continue through the night. “According to the information we have so far, there were around 15 to 20 people on the boat. Of them, 11, all minors aged around 15, have died. Seven people, including the boat owner, have been rescued. We are carrying out rescue operations, which will continue throughout the night,” Singh said. Initial reports suggested that around 25 to 30 people were aboard the medium-sized boat, most of them travelling to attend a feast organised as part of Hindu funeral rituals. The boat was “ferrying passengers from one hamlet to another along the river” when it overturned, a senior police official told HT. Officials said the vessel capsized after becoming unbalanced, while some passengers managed to swim to safety. Locals who witnessed the incident rushed to help and alerted the administration. Several children were taken to a primary health centre by locals, where a doctor examined them and declared them dead. Their families were inconsolable, with relatives breaking down in tears. Singh said the boat was owned by a local resident who had used it to ferry villagers to a feast in a nearby village. “The boat owner has claimed there were 15 to 20 people on board. We are still verifying the facts,” she said. The district magistrate added that boat operations at night were restricted and that the incident would be investigated. Teams from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) are searching the river for the missing passengers. Darkness and the depth of the water have hampered rescue efforts. Bihar CM announces ₹ 4 lakh ex gratia for kin Chief minister Samrat Choudhary, in an X post on his official handle, described the deaths of minors in boat capsize as heart-wrenching and saddening. The CM has announced that families of the deceased would be given ₹ four lakh each as ex gratia and has directed the administration to conduct rescue operations and ensure that the injured get best of medicare. Opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav in his official X handle described the incident as tragic and unfortunate. He wrote " tragic and unfortunate news has been received of a boat capsizing in the Raghopur Diara area. Most of those who drowned were children. May God keep everyone safe. A directive has been issued to coordinate with local people, the administration and officials to speed up relief, rescue and treatment operations". Yadav's represents the Raghopur assembly constituency, one of the riverine areas in Vaishali district. Boat capsized in Bihar’s Samastipur Earlier this year, at least three people died and four went missing after a boat carrying 14 passengers capsized in the Ganga near Sultanpur Diara in Bihar’s Samastipur district in May. Seven passengers were rescued safely, officials said. The passengers, all residents of Bind Toli in Masoomganj under Patna district’s Barh police station area, had travelled to Sultanpur Diara for agricultural work. They were returning to Umanath Ghat with vegetables harvested from parwal fields when the boat overturned. Mohiuddin Nagar circle officer Brijesh Kumar Dwivedi confirmed three deaths, saying the deceased included two men and one woman. Officials have established the identities of all three victims. The Patna district administration said the boat departed from Bind Toli around 5.45 am with 14 people on board. The passengers regularly crossed the river to work in agricultural fields. An initial update from the administration said seven people had been rescued, two bodies recovered and five passengers were missing. Officials cited strong winds as a possible cause of the accident, while Barh sub-divisional officer Garima Lohiya said the boat’s engine failed midstream. Rescue teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), along with the Patna and Samastipur district administrations, took part in the operation. As news of the accident spread, local residents and relatives gathered at Umanath Ghat. Authorities continued the search for the missing passengers and carried out procedures related to the recovered bodies. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Avinash Kumar Avinash, a senior correspondent, reports on crime, railways, defence and social sector, with specialisation in police, home department and other investigation agencies.

news.headline: Opposition announces ‘mission to restore democracy’, plans India Plus group
news.story_lead: Opposition announces ‘mission to restore democracy’, plans India Plus group Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition would challenge the Centre’s decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a protest site, vowing to defend people’s democratic rights The Opposition parties on Tuesday announced a “mission to restore democracy”, vowing to intensify their political fight against the Union government’s decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. The parties also agreed to wait for the Supreme Court’s response to their petition filed on Monday before organising another massive march in the heart of Delhi. The Opposition leaders described Monday’s march to the Supreme Court as a significant achievement and decided to form an “INDIA Plus” group to bring together political parties, activists, students and other organisations.
news.full_article_text: Opposition announces ‘mission to restore democracy’, plans India Plus group Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition would challenge the Centre’s decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a protest site, vowing to defend people’s democratic rights The Opposition parties on Tuesday announced a “mission to restore democracy”, vowing to intensify their political fight against the Union government’s decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. The parties also agreed to wait for the Supreme Court’s response to their petition filed on Monday before organising another massive march in the heart of Delhi. The Opposition leaders described Monday’s march to the Supreme Court as a significant achievement and decided to form an “INDIA Plus” group to bring together political parties, activists, students and other organisations. They also discussed a tentative plan to organise a mock Parliament, while Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi urged the leaders to remain prepared for “surprise movements”. “We are all standing here together as one. As I said yesterday, there are no parallel protests. There is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: restoration of democracy in India,” Gandhi told the media after the meeting. Deep Dive ALSO READ | SIR row: Amit Shah says 'Congress losing since decades'; party flags ‘heights of irony’ “Democracy has been destroyed in this country. The election system has been destroyed. The Constitution has been torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule, genuine democratic rule in this country,” he said. Gandhi said Jantar Mantar had been a place where people could express their democratic aspirations, but the government had now decided that it could no longer be used for that purpose. “Well, we are going to challenge that idea. It is not going to be so simple for the government to decide that the Indian people will not fight for their voice. The people who have done this, they need to understand that the net is closing around them. It is not going to be so simple that you can destroy the Indian Constitution and get away with it,” he added. Gandhi also thanked the people of Delhi and other parts of the country for supporting Monday’s march, saying the mobilisation reflected public sentiment rather than merely the efforts of political parties. We were there, but what happened yesterday could not have happened without the expression of the average citizen of this country, non-political citizen of this country,” he said. He added that the Opposition wanted to thank the people who had stood with them against the government’s decision. “This is not about us, this is about the people of India, this is about the future of the people of India. And we, all of us together, because we love you and we respect you are going to fight to the end to restore the democratic process in this country. It is our commitment, the people who have done this, are going to be brought to justice,” Gandhi said. Oppn to await SC response before next mega march The meeting, which lasted more than two hours, saw several leaders criticise the government’s decision to remove Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest sites. The Union Home Ministry has notified Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as designated protest sites. It was among the rare occasions in recent times when Gandhi hosted Opposition leaders for a tea meeting at his official residence at 5, Sunehri Bagh Road. Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah, Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chief Mehbooba Mufti, Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leaders Tejashwi Yadav and Manoj Jha, and Samajwadi Party leaders Anand Bhadauria, Harender Malik and M Nadvi were also present. Other attendees included Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader Mahua Maji, Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary MA Baby, Communist Party of India (CPI) general secretary D Raja and party MP Sandosh Kumar, Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation leader Dipankar Bhattacharya, and Forward Bloc leader G Devarajan. Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) MP Supriya Sule, Kerala Congress leader Jose K Mani and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) leader Thol Thirumavalavan also participated in the meeting. All India Students’ Association (AISA) chief Neha Bora, Students’ Federation of India (SFI) leader Aishee Ghosh, and activists Yogendra Yadav and Prashant Bhushan were among those present. According to three senior leaders who attended the meeting, the participants reviewed Monday’s march to the Supreme Court and expressed satisfaction with the scale of mobilisation. “It has been decided that before taking out another massive march in the heart of Delhi, the INDIA bloc will wait for the Supreme Court’s view on our petition. The logic is that we have already gone to the court so we must wait for the SC’s orders,” a senior leader said. However, the decision to await the court’s response will not prevent Opposition parties from continuing their protests at Jantar Mantar, the leaders indicated. “Our decentralised programmes will continue to take place in Jantar Mantar. We do not agree with the government’s view that protests can’t be held at that place,” another leader said. Mock Parliament, surprise protests discussed According to functionaries who attended the meeting, the leaders also discussed a preliminary plan to organise a mock Parliament targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Gandhi also urged the leaders to remain alert for “surprise movements” that could be organised at short notice, including within 24 hours. MA Baby criticised the government over the decision concerning Jantar Mantar, drawing a parallel with the Opposition’s allegations of electoral malpractice. “After vote chori, the government has even done ‘chori of Jantar Mantar’,” Baby said. “Gyanesh Kumar has joined the ruling party’s team... news.headline: Five arrested as 29-year-old man dies after ‘assault’ over beer spill at north Delhi nightclub
news.story_lead: Five arrested as 29-year-old man dies after ‘assault’ over beer spill at north Delhi nightclub Police are examining CCTV footage and allegations of a firearm threat and theft as they investigate the death of Daljeet at Tor House nightclub. A probe into the death of a 29-year-old man following an alleged assault at a north Delhi nightclub has led to five arrests, including the establishment’s manager, his wife and three bouncers, police said on Tuesday. The incident occurred late on October 10 at Tor House, near Ashok Park Metro station in the Sarai Rohilla police station area.
news.full_article_text: Five arrested as 29-year-old man dies after ‘assault’ over beer spill at north Delhi nightclub Police are examining CCTV footage and allegations of a firearm threat and theft as they investigate the death of Daljeet at Tor House nightclub. A probe into the death of a 29-year-old man following an alleged assault at a north Delhi nightclub has led to five arrests, including the establishment’s manager, his wife and three bouncers, police said on Tuesday. The incident occurred late on October 10 at Tor House, near Ashok Park Metro station in the Sarai Rohilla police station area. The deceased, Daljeet, lived in Raghuvir Nagar with his wife, Pooja, their eight-year-old son and his father. Investigators are looking into a dispute that allegedly broke out after beer spilled on the club manager’s wife while Daljeet was at the venue with five to six friends, according to police. Also Read: 29-Year-Old Man Allegedly Beaten To Death By Club Bouncers Over Beer Spill Row | HT India The disagreement reportedly escalated when bouncers became involved. Daljeet’s friends alleged that the group apologised but was nevertheless attacked. They claimed the assault involved sticks and glass bottles and continued even after they asked the attackers to stop. The group also alleged that attempts to leave the premises were unsuccessful, with bouncers allegedly pulling them back inside and assaulting them again. Water was reportedly poured on the men during the incident. Daljeet suffered serious injuries, including a fractured jaw, his friends said. After managing to leave the club, his companions took him to his residence in Raghuvir Nagar. He collapsed near the entrance, according to the account provided by his friends, and was subsequently taken to Guru Gobind Singh Hospital , where doctors declared him dead. Sunny, one of Daljeet’s friends who sustained a minor head injury, said he received a call from Pooja following the incident. He alleged that footage of the assault was captured by the nightclub’s surveillance cameras and called for strict action against those involved. The group has raised other allegations, including that one of the accused displayed a firearm and that cash and two mobile phones were taken from them. Police are examining these claims as part of the ongoing investigation. Also Read: Woman allegedly stripped, beaten at Guwahati club after drunken brawl with bouncers To establish how the incident unfolded, investigators have taken possession of the nightclub’s digital video recorder (DVR) and are reviewing the CCTV footage. The exercise is also intended to help determine whether additional people were involved. The investigation is also examining a separate allegation by the family concerning the police response. The family claimed that a police response vehicle arrived outside the club after a call was made to the control room but left without conducting an inquiry. Police are additionally checking whether Tor House had the necessary permissions to operate late at night. Records have been sought from the Excise Department and the Licensing Branch in connection with the inquiry. Police are continuing to investigate the dispute, the alleged assault and the circumstances surrounding Daljeet’s death.
