news.headline: Mangrove Army: How Sundarbans’ ‘tiger widows’ are protecting the forest, one sapling a time
news.story_lead: Mangrove Army: How Sundarbans’ ‘tiger widows’ are protecting the forest, one sapling a time Known as the “Mangrove Army”, the group was recently praised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Mann Ki Baat address aired on September 27 An ‘army’ of women, many of whom have lost their husbands in tiger attacks, known as ‘tiger widows’, are now fighting to save the Sundarbans in West Bengal, the world’s largest mangrove delta and home to more than 100 tigers. Known as the “Mangrove Army”, the group was recently praised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Mann Ki Baat address aired on September 27. The women plant mangrove saplings along riverbanks to protect their villages from cyclones and help conserve the fragile ecosystem.
news.full_article_text: Mangrove Army: How Sundarbans’ ‘tiger widows’ are protecting the forest, one sapling a time Known as the “Mangrove Army”, the group was recently praised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Mann Ki Baat address aired on September 27 An ‘army’ of women, many of whom have lost their husbands in tiger attacks, known as ‘tiger widows’, are now fighting to save the Sundarbans in West Bengal, the world’s largest mangrove delta and home to more than 100 tigers. Known as the “Mangrove Army”, the group was recently praised by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Mann Ki Baat address aired on September 27. The women plant mangrove saplings along riverbanks to protect their villages from cyclones and help conserve the fragile ecosystem. Namita Kayal, 45, a resident of Lahiripur, a remote island in the Sundarbans, lost her husband to a tiger attack in 2021. He was killed while catching crabs in the creeks inside the forest. Her sister-in-law, Anita Kayal, lost her husband in a similar attack in 2017. The two women now work with the Mangrove Army, planting mangrove saplings along the riverbanks that separate their village from the forest inhabited by tigers. The group provides them with essential household supplies in return for their work. Also Read: Green tribunal impleads BMC in mangrove-dumping case in Diva “My sister-in-law and I have both lost our husbands in tiger attacks. They were the only earning members of our families. Now, we both work for the Mangrove Army. We receive ration and other items for planting mangroves on the muddy banks. There are many others in the group like us who have lost their husbands in tiger attacks,” Namita told HT over the phone. The group that is now called the ‘Mangrove Army’ was formed in 2009, after cyclone Aila devastated the Sundarbans, by Umashankar Mondal, a government schoolteacher in West Bengal. He brought together around 200 village women to plant mangrove saplings along riverbanks. Over the years, the initiative has grown to include around 600 women, of whom approximately 120 have lost their husbands in tiger attacks. “Since 2009, we have planted more than 1.3 million mangrove saplings along the riverbanks of 12 remote islands, including Satjelia, Kumirmari and Choto Mollakhali. We have been working silently all these years, away from the focus of mainstream media. It was only in July 2023 that we officially named the women’s group the ‘Mangrove Army’. It was recently highlighted by the Prime Minister,” said Mondal, secretary of the Purbasha Eco-helpline Society, the non-profit organisation behind the initiative. Also Read: 4.5-acre mangrove forest to make way for Tata Power switching station The women, ranging in age from 25 to over 60, wade through knee-deep mud along riverbanks to plant thousands of saplings every year. They do not receive wages for their work but are provided with essential supplies to support their families. “In return, we don’t get any money. Instead, we receive everyday items needed to run the family — rice, dal, cooking oil and spices. Sometimes, we also get sarees, sanitary napkins, seeds to grow vegetables, fish fingerlings for our ponds and chickens for poultry. Recently, the society organised free eye-testing camps, and those who needed spectacles were provided with them,” Anita said. In his Mann Ki Baat address, PM Modi praised the women for restoring the mangrove forests despite the personal losses they suffered. “In the Sundarbans of West Bengal, some women are setting an inspiring example of the special bond [that humans share] with nature. These women are growing and restoring mangrove forests. Many of these women lost their husbands in tiger attacks. After losing their husbands, they got support for their livelihood from the Sundarbans. The mangroves they had planted have now become a natural shield for the villages. They are also earning by planting these mangroves,” Modi said. Also Read: Sunderban crocodiles losing their nesting grounds due to climate change: Govt report The Sundarbans comprises around 102 islands, of which only 52 are inhabited. The remaining islands are home to national parks, tiger reserves and wildlife sanctuaries. The region is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mangroves serve as a natural barrier against cyclones, helping protect coastal settlements from storm surges and strong winds. The Sundarbans also acts as a buffer for Kolkata, located around 100km to the northwest, against cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal. However, the region’s mangrove cover remains vulnerable. Data from the Forest Survey of India (FSI) show that while the overall mangrove cover in the Sundarbans increased marginally between 2019 and 2021, the gains were largely driven by an expansion in open mangrove cover, which primarily includes plantations. According to the FSI’s 2021 report, the total mangrove cover in the Sundarbans, including very dense, moderately dense and open mangroves, increased from 2,112 sq km in 2019 to 2,114 sq km in 2021. The moderately dense mangrove cover remained unchanged during the period. Tiger attacks, meanwhile, continue to pose a risk to people who enter the forest to earn a living. Senior officials said such fatalities have declined over the years. At least 15 people were killed in tiger attacks in 2018, while no deaths were recorded in 2023 and one was reported in 2024. Some deaths may go unreported when villagers enter the forest without permission. For Namita, the Prime Minister’s recognition has brought long-awaited attention to the women’s efforts on the remote islands. “The Prime Minister himself flagged our work. It came as a huge achievement for us who work on the remote islands trying to save the Sundarbans and their villages,” she said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Joydeep Thakur Joydeep Thakur is a Special Correspondent based in Kolkata. He focuses on science, environment, wildlife, agriculture and other related issues.

news.headline: Thousands march to Indian Supreme Court to demand election chief resign
news.story_lead: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend.
news.full_article_text: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi submitted a petition to the court challenging the process, in which tens of millions of names have been struck off the voter rolls. Opposition parties allege the revision benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. For weeks requests to protest had been denied by police, citing law and order reasons. Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained in Delhi. Gandhi called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march. In a press conference, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to Chief Justice Surya Kant, laying out their concerns with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged conduct. After they filed their petition later in the day, Kant responded by saying the matter was already before the court and therefore sub judice - meaning he could not speak about it. But he added: "You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law." There was a heavy security deployment in central Delhi and along the route of the march, with restrictions on traffic and on entry and exit at some metro stations. A bus carrying Gandhi and other opposition leaders made its way to the court from Barakamba road. Supporters waved flags and chanted his name as the Congress MP and others waved through the windows. Seated a few rows behind him was Neha Bora, a student leader who has gained prominence in the protests. A few kilometres on, in a place called Mandi House, the bus stopped and Rahul Gandhi and a few others climbed on top of the vehicle to wave at supporters lining up the street in the thousands. Many protesters climbed on to other buses parked here, while some waved flags and chanted anti-government slogans to the sound of drums and lots of cheering. "If they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?" one protester asked an AFP news agency reporter. Another protester called the march "a fight to save the very fabric" of India, the world's largest democracy. Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday Protesters have been demanding the country's the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud Over the past week, top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, have been briefly detained several times while leading protests in central Delhi. On Sunday, the CJP - which is not a registered political party - said it would continue protesting until Kumar stepped down. The CJP, which successfully led a protest over the summer that culminated in India's federal education minister's resignation, had called for a march on Saturday to Jantar Mantar - the best-known protest site in Delhi where the last set of sit-in demonstrations had also happened. But authorities in Delhi imposed overarching restrictions that made it almost impossible for protesters to travel and reach Jantar Mantar - trains were cancelled, dozens of metro stations were shut and tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were on the roads to detain protesters. The Home Ministry has now announced demonstrations will no longer be permitted at Jantar Mantar. Three other sites have been listed as alternatives should permission be granted. Monday's demonstrations come after thousands were detained over the weekend The CJP leaders - founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - were dramatically detained from a plane as they landed in Delhi to join the weekend protest. They were only released a day later - while Dipke returned home to attend his grandmother's funeral, Das and Ranka held a press conference where they said the protests would continue. Both leaders have said they will seek a new protest date from the police. Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses. Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday denied being pushed by leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi during a protest march to Supreme Court. The INDIA bloc held a march on Monday seeking Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Shivakumar said that Rahul Gandhi didn't push him aside, but was only concerned for him because the crowd was massive. "Rahul Gandhi did not push me during the protest held in Delhi. "No one pushed me during the protest," he asserted, while taking a swipe at the BJP, saying it had "immense affection" for him and was therefore spreading "misinformation". Sharing the video, the Karnataka BJP said Kannadigas will never forgive Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party. “Preventing him (Shivakumar) from approaching Rahul Gandhi and pushing him away in such an inhumane manner is a grave insult to the entire state of Karnataka by the Congress party. Kannadigas will never forgive Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party,” the party said in a tweet. "From Rajiv Gandhi unceremoniously announcing Veerendra Patil's removal as Karnataka CM at an airport to Rahul Gandhi pulling D K Shivakumar by his kurta in the middle of a road, the Congress dynasty's sense of entitlement remains unchanged," he posted on 'X'. Earlier, Karnataka Deputy CM G Parameshwara also dismissed allegations of Gandhi deliberately pushing Shivakumar and said that crowd control during protests is challenging. "During a protest, crowd control is not easy. The primary responsibility of the security personnel there was to protect Rahul Gandhi and ensure that people could not easily approach him. news.story_lead: Odisha Cabinet approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students, ₹500-crore urban drainage scheme Odisha Cabinet approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students, ₹ 500-crore urban drainage scheme Bhubaneswar, Oct13 The Odisha government on Tuesday approved free textbooks for around 28.7 lakh students of state-run schools, along with a ₹ 500-crore programme to improve urban drainage and tackle flooding. The decisions were among 16 proposals approved at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi here. The proposals, relating to 11 departments, will be implemented soon, Chief Secretary Anu Garg told reporters after the meeting.
news.full_article_text: Odisha Cabinet approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students, ₹500-crore urban drainage scheme Odisha Cabinet approves free textbooks for 28.7 lakh students, ₹ 500-crore urban drainage scheme Bhubaneswar, Oct13 The Odisha government on Tuesday approved free textbooks for around 28.7 lakh students of state-run schools, along with a ₹ 500-crore programme to improve urban drainage and tackle flooding. The decisions were among 16 proposals approved at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi here. The proposals, relating to 11 departments, will be implemented soon, Chief Secretary Anu Garg told reporters after the meeting. The decision to provide free textbooks to more students comes amid a controversy over the supply of textbooks containing errors, with opposition parties demanding the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond. Garg said students of classes 9 and 10 in government and government-aided secondary schools, other than those covered under the existing SC and ST provisions, would now receive free textbooks. The scheme aims to ensure equitable access to quality education, reduce the financial burden on economically weaker families, improve enrolment in government schools, lower dropout rates and increase the transition from elementary to secondary education. Students belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes were already receiving free textbooks, she said. "The scheme will remain in force for five years, from 2025-26 to 2029-30, with a total estimated outlay of ₹ 284.07 crore, covering a tentative 28.7 lakh beneficiaries," Garg said. The procurement of paper, printing, transportation and distribution of textbooks will be undertaken through a transparent and competitive process in accordance with the Odisha General Financial Rules and applicable procurement guidelines, she said. The School and Mass Education Department will put in place a mechanism to collect, verify and validate beneficiary data through field-level verification. It will also ensure that textbooks are printed and supplied to schools well before the commencement of each academic session, Garg said. Over 1,600 mistakes, including spelling errors and incorrect names of eminent personalities, were found in 55 textbooks supplied by the department. In another major decision, the Cabinet approved the Urban Storm Water Drainage Management and Improvement Programme , with an outlay of ₹ 500 crore from the state's own resources over a period of five years, from 2026-27 to 2030-31. The scheme will cover urban local bodies and selected block headquarters. The proposed interventions include desilting, construction of reinforced cement concrete stormwater drains, covering of drains, restoration of natural drainage channels and their linkage with suitable water bodies. The measures are aimed at improving the capacity and efficiency of urban drainage systems and reducing waterlogging and localised flooding, Garg said. The programme is also expected to promote groundwater recharge, improve public safety and environmental quality, and support climate-resilient urban development. The Cabinet also approved the establishment of a Disaster Recovery-cum-Data Centre at Keonjhar to ensure the uninterrupted functioning of critical government digital services during major disruptions, including earthquakes and cyclones. The Odisha State Data Centre in Bhubaneswar hosts critical government applications, databases and platforms supporting government-to-government, government-to-business and government-to-citizen services. The proposed facility at Keonjhar will serve as a disaster recovery centre, enabling the state to protect its data and maintain essential services in the event of a major disruption at the Bhubaneswar facility. "Both Keonjhar and Bhubaneswar are located in different seismic zones. If there is any damage in Bhubaneswar, data could remain safe at the Keonjhar centre," Garg said. The project will cost over ₹ 176 crore, including capital expenditure of ₹ 154 crore and operational expenditure of ₹ 22.83 crore for five years. An amount of ₹ 162.83 crore has been provided from the Fifth State Finance Commission grant-in-aid, she said. The state Cabinet also approved a tender worth ₹ 105 crore for the construction of an in-stream water storage project on the Tel river at Tustapali village in Bolangir district. The project is expected to strengthen water security and help mitigate chronic water scarcity in the drought-prone district. Apart from these proposals, the Cabinet approved measures relating to the Fisheries and Animal Resources Development; Industries, Skill Development and Technical Education; Finance; Electronics and Information Technology; Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment; Housing and Urban Development; Revenue and Disaster Management; Water Resources; and School and Mass Education departments.
